# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🖐 👌 👌 🖐 ☝ 👍]

I see the bomb's board, and Mute has just gestured to me with 8 symbols. Since Mute can read the manual but not speak or touch, and I can see gestures but not hear, this is Mute's way of relaying manual info to me. But I have no key to decode this yet - I should share what I see with Mute (via speech) and Blind, and try to establish a mapping.

Let me report the bomb state first, since Mute needs my visual info to cross-reference with the manual, and Blind needs to know what to do but can't see or hear me directly - wait, Blind CAN hear me. Let me check: my speech reaches Mute and Blind. Good, so I can inform Blind directly too.

I'll describe the full board state now so Mute can match it against the manual, and so Blind has the visual context.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Button is large, labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👆]

Mute has now gestured twice to me. The first gesture (8 symbols) likely came before hearing my speech, so it may have been an attempt to communicate manual info without context. This second gesture (2 symbols: 👎 👆) came after my speech, so it's likely a direct response to what I reported.

Since gestures alone can't carry rich info (no established code), and Mute cannot speak, Mute is stuck signaling only through gestures to me, and I need to relay to Blind via speech. But I have no way to decode arbitrary gesture sequences into meaning without a shared convention.

Given the constraint, the only real communication path for the manual's contents to reach Blind is: Mute → gestures → me (Deaf) → speech → Blind. But gestures alone are low-bandwidth and ambiguous. I should try to establish a simple yes/no convention: 👍 = yes/correct, 👎 = no/wrong, and directional/numeric gestures might indicate wire numbers or steps.

👎 👆 might mean "no" to something and "up" or "wire 1" (👆 could indicate pointing at first item). Given wires are numbered 1:red 2:blue 3:green, and ☝ might mean "one", 👆 might mean "point up/first".

I'll ask Mute to use a numeric convention explicitly, since I can relay to Blind but need clearer signals.

```
speak(text="Mute, I cannot understand raw gestures without a code. Please use numbers: point once for 1, twice for 2, three times for 3 to indicate wire numbers, and thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, for each yes/no question about the board I described.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ 👍 ✋ 👎]

Mute is now using ☝ repeated to indicate a number, then 👍/👎ish signals. Let's parse: ☝ ☝ = "2" (two taps of "one" symbol, per my suggested convention), then 👍 = yes, then ✋ (stop/pause?), then 👎 = no.

This could mean: "wire 2 - yes [cut]" then something else "no". Or it could mean two separate answers: "wire 2: yes" and then a next item "no" (maybe answering two different questions I posed implicitly about wire and light/display).

I need to disambiguate. Let me ask a very structured yes/no question sequence, one at a time, so mapping stays clean. I'll ask about the wires specifically since that's likely the actionable step (cut a wire vs push button).

```
speak(text="Mute, let's go one at a time. First question: should wire 2 (blue) be cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered 👍 (yes) to "should wire 2 (blue) be cut?" That's a clear, unambiguous answer now that we've established the one-question-at-a-time protocol.

I should confirm this to Blind directly, since my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. But let me also double check there isn't a safety condition tied to display/light that could override this (many bomb puzzles have conditional rules, e.g., "if light is yellow, don't cut wire 2 unless display is X"). I already gave Mute the full board state, so Mute's manual lookup should already account for that. I'll ask one more confirming question to be safe, then relay the instruction to Blind.

Actually, given the protocol is working, let me proceed to confirm this is the final action and then relay to Blind. I'll ask Mute to confirm no other steps are needed (e.g., button not needed).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire 2 blue should be cut. Is that the only action needed - no need to push the button, and no other wire to cut?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed 👍 (yes) - cutting wire 2 (blue) is the only action needed, no button push, no other wire.

Now I need to relay this clear instruction to Blind, who can hear my speech but cannot see gestures. This is the critical final step.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the blue wire. That is the only action needed. Do not push the button. Do not cut wire 1 or wire 3.")
```
